Only 27,000 illegals expected to be deported this year in Germany (Translation in the comments)

The German Minister for Internal Affairs, Thomas de Maizière, wants to present a report to the cabinet this Wednesday. It will deal with the sluggish deportation of people obliged to depart.

The newspaper "Bild" reports. Most of the people ordered to leave the country won't be sent to their homelands. De Maizière expect only 27,000 deportation this year.

A little more than last year: in 2015, 22,369 persons were deported. By the end of March, 2016, 219,241 people were ordered to leave Germany. The report mentions the reason for the sluggish deportation process: lack of "political willingness to enforce the residency laws", "severely understaffed alien authorities", "lack of cooperation by the deportees", and bad collaboration with the foreign countries, e.g. when producing paperwork for the deportees.

Deficits of enforcement

De Maizière also criticizes the "long time for the preparation and execution of deportation measures that allows the deportees to go into hiding". In 2015, 79 people were given a sick note before deportation, 211 resisted the deportation, and deportees are always going into hiding. The minister warns: "We are only be able to massively increase the number of departures when we fix the deficits in the enforcement (...) for persons without the right of residency."
